title: Patient Care Desk Guidance: Claim Correction Amount on Declined Controlled Balances
content:
When a patient declines the owed balance of a Kestrel Prescriptions record in the Schedule V Controlled Prescription, Schedule III-IV Controlled Prescription or Schedule II Controlled Prescription class, the plan's claim for the controlled short fill has to be corrected, and the controlled rebill amount is kept for it. The claim reversal deadline comes from the patient's active plan under Prescription Insurance on File.

## The rule

The controlled rebill amount looks at how the plan's claim for the controlled short fill is corrected, counting calendar days from its dispensing date, as day 0, to today:

- an insurance-billed short fill declined **more than** the active plan's claim reversal deadline days after its dispensing date keeps **0.75**;
- an insurance-billed short fill declined **within** that many days keeps **0.25**;
- any other short fill keeps nothing.

The rebill amount is taken off the controlled unpaid value, and the unpaid value after what is kept is never below zero.

## Both sides (hypothetical plan with a claim reversal deadline of 14 days, short fill dispensed on day 0)

| Payment of the short fill | Declined on | Rebill amount kept |
|---|---|---|
| billed to insurance | day 14 | 0.25 (within 14 days) |
| billed to insurance | day 15 | 0.75 (more than 14 days) |
| billed to insurance | day 0 | 0.25 |
| discount program or cash | any day | nothing |
